newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: NO MORE SURVIVORS IN AUSTRALIAN LANDSLIDE-RESCUERS.
newsitem.headline: NO MORE SURVIVORS IN AUSTRALIAN LANDSLIDE-RESCUERS.

text.p: Rescuers on Thursday recovered the body of the last known victim from a landslide that claimed 18 lives at this popular Australian ski village a week ago.

There was only one survivor, ski instructor Stuart Diver, 27, who was trapped between slabs of broken concrete and was hauled to safety on Saturday after three nights of being drenched by running water in freezing temperatures.

Working in heavy rain on the scarred, heavily developed mountainside at Thredbo, in the Snowy Mountains south of Canberra, exhausted rescuers unearthed the 18th body, a man, from the hopelessly compacted rubble of two ski lodges at about 2 a.m. (1600 GMT on Wednesday).
Police called the search and rescue effort a success, saying it had been too much to hope for another survivor as lucky and mentally tough as Diver.
"It was a massive bonus," police superintendent Eric Gollan said of Diver's miraculous escape.
"It was only professionalism that got that person out as a survivor," he told reporters at Thredbo.
Meanwhile, rescuers who had picked their way gingerly through the unstable slope for seven days prepared before dawn to clear the disaster scene with heavy machinery, but were hampered by the rain.
"We are reasonably confident we have explored any cavities that are there. It was just an absolute miracle that that cavity (where Diver lay trapped for three days) formed," Gollan said.
Diver's wife, Sally, was one of the 18 who died. They were in bed together when their lodge was engulfed near midnight in a cascade of concrete, twisted metal, trees, dirt and boulders.
The discovery of all the missing bodies brought an end to a distressing vigil kept up at the scene by family of the dead. All the relatives were now able to mourn their loved ones.
Diver continued his rapid recovery from frostbite this week and was back on his feet again at a hospital in Canberra.
